results.title: Simulation in Clinical Trials: The Strategic Stage
results.content: The FDA’s 2019 guidance on adaptive designs emphasizes improving “statistical efficiency of trial operating characteristics (e.g., type I error rates and power)” through innovative designs ( Recent innovations in adaptive trial designs: A review of design opportunities in translational research - PMC ) – and reaching that efficiency almost always involves simulation. We will drill down into operating characteristic simulations (to assess power and error rates), Bayesian predictive simulations (for forecasting trial outcomes and go/no-go decisions), adaptive trial simulations (covering group sequential designs, sample size re-estimation, adaptive randomization, etc.), simulations for sensitivity analyses (stress-testing assumptions), dropout modeling, and treatment effect heterogeneity. Also, the R package rpact (available on CRAN and GitHub) is a comprehensive tool for adaptive design simulations – it can calculate power, sample size, simulate various endpoints, and even handle multi-arm and enrichment designs (GitHub - rpact-com/rpact: rpact: Confirmatory Adaptive Clinical Trial Design and Analysis).
